topic: IBM 2026 CHRO study: executives rank supervising and overriding AI far above what employees do
title: The AI skill your boss ranks first

source.title: Designing the Thinking Organization (2026 CHRO Study)

body:
71% of bosses rank overruling AI above using it. Only 38% of their staff agree.

That gap is from IBM's new study of 1,500 HR chiefs and 8,800 employees, run April to June 2026.

Everyone is learning to prompt. Almost nobody is practising the thing employers rank first: catching the answer that is wrong.

It gets sharper. 60% of employees say their own skills are slipping, and the one they name most is critical thinking. Only 26% of companies have written down which decisions stay human.

So the scarce skill next year is not speed. It is being the person who can say: this output is wrong, and here is how I know.

Today, take one AI answer you accepted this week and find the part you cannot verify. That is your gap.
action: take one AI answer you accepted this week and find the part you cannot verify
first_comment: Source: IBM Institute for Business Value, "Designing the Thinking Organization" (2026 CHRO Study), published 21 Sep 2026 — https://www.ibm.com/thought-leadership/institute-business-value/en-us/report/2026-chro

pages.headline: Your boss ranks overruling AI above using it
pages.deck: IBM asked 1,500 HR chiefs and 8,800 employees which skill matters most. They disagree by 33 points.

pages.label: Executives who rank supervising and overriding AI first
pages.body: Among employees, 38% say the same. A 33-point gap on the one skill the people who write job descriptions rank highest.

pages.headline: Prompting is not the scarce skill
pages.body: Prompt tips are everywhere and cost nothing to copy. Knowing when the answer is wrong is the thing the survey says employers are short of.

pages.headline: Your own skills are slipping quietly
pages.body: 60% of employees told IBM they worry their skills are eroding. The one they name most often is critical thinking, the exact skill being asked for.

pages.headline: Two ways to use the same tool
pages.left: Accept the draft, send it on, hope the numbers hold up.
pages.right: Check the claim that carries the risk, then send it with a note on what you checked.

pages.headline: Most firms never drew the line
pages.body: Only 26% clearly define which work is human-led and which is AI-assisted. Until that is written down, the person who overrides the model carries the risk alone.

pages.quote: Employees stop deferring to the machine and start supervising it.
pages.body: Where HR shares ownership of that boundary, 76% of those organisations report staff feel safe to question or override AI.

pages.label: Do this today
pages.headline: Find the part you cannot verify
pages.body: Take one AI answer you accepted this week. Mark the claim that would cost most if it were wrong. Check that one. The habit is the skill.

pages.headline: One idea, decoded, every week
pages.body: Plain English, a named source, and one thing to do with it.
